subject: Urgent: Acme production 99th pct latency spikes — immediate triage requested
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.health>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Platform Ops <platform-ops@acme.health>, ctofinance@acme.health
Date: 2026-05-18T16:05:22Z
Subject: Production: 99th+ latency spikes and 504s since 22:00 UTC

Sean —

We're seeing a sustained increase in 95th/99th latency and intermittent 504s in our production integration starting around 2026-05-17 22:00 UTC. Impact: our clinical ingestion pipeline is timing out for a subset of large batched requests (~3-6% of traffic), and overall throughput has dropped by ~18% for the last 6 hours.

I've attached a small digest (acme_latency_digest_20260517.csv) and a representative HAR. Key observations from my team:
- 99th percentile token latency jumped from ~240ms to ~1.4s after 22:00 UTC
- Error rate (504/timeouts) rose from 0.1% to 3.2% for requests > 1k tokens
- The errors are cross-region (us-east and us-west) but concentrated on your managed shard IDs listed in the CSV

This is causing customer-facing failures for our clinicians. We need an immediate triage and a mitigation plan (temporary capacity increase, rollback, or fallback to smaller model). Please escalate to engineering and provide an ETA for a remediation. Acme is reserving the right to pause live traffic if we don't have a mitigation in 2 hours.

Thanks — please loop in whoever you need.

— Samantha
Samantha Lee
VP, Platform Engineering, Acme Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-18T16:45:33Z
Subject: Re: Production: 99th+ latency spikes and 504s since 22:00 UTC

Team — initial triage notes (15:45 UTC):

What we see so far:
- There is a tail-latency pattern consistent with queueing/backpressure on a subset of model shards (shard-17, shard-18). Metrics link: https://console.redwood.ai/metrics/shards/shard-17?range=6h
- Around 22:00 UTC yesterday we pushed a platform-wide change to strict per-tenant concurrency caps (to reduce noisy-neighbor amplification). The new cap reduces max concurrent inferences per tenant from 48 -> 32 per shard.
- Observed behavior: bursts above 32 concurrent requests per tenant are queuing and causing exponential head-of-line blocking on requests that are already large (long prompt + streaming).
- The backlog triggering path appears for requests with large context (>1k tokens) and where clients are using streaming + function-calls; KV-cache warmups also contribute.

Immediate mitigations proposed (we can apply now):
- TEMP: bump Acme's per-tenant concurrency from 32 -> 64 for the next 2 hours (manual override) — low-risk, requires a config flip (15s to apply).
- TEMP: enable model-fallback routing for requests exceeding 800 token input to small-variant (model-small-v2) with degraded-cost billing — avoids queueing on large-model shards.
- Flush per-tenant prefix cache for Acme to remove stale KV entries that are causing larger inference token counts for some paths (30s operation).
- Add tight request-id sampling on the bridge to capture stacktraces and runtime queueing latency for the next 2 hours.

Longer-term follow-ups:
- Revisit concurrency cap algorithm: move from flat cap -> adaptive cap based on historical tail distribution and request size buckets.
- Add explicit per-tenant queuing metrics and alerting (95/99 tail queues) and a runbook for auto-bump/rollback.

I’m starting the temporary overrides now and will report back once applied; Evelyn will confirm if any data-plane knobs are blocking the change.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Redwood Leadership <leadership@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.health>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-19T09:12:05Z
Subject: Exec summary: Acme latency spike — root cause and next steps

Leadership — quick summary and ask for visibility: 

What happened: A platform change on 2026-05-17 22:00 UTC lowered per-tenant concurrency caps (48 -> 32) to mitigate noisy neighbors. The cap surfaced unexpected head-of-line queueing for large requests from Acme, producing a sustained increase in 95/99 tail latency and a spike in 504s.

What we did:
- Applied temporary override to increase Acme concurrency to 64 (2026-05-18 16:50 UTC) — immediate reduction in 99th latency for captured samples
- Enabled fallback routing to model-small-v2 for input > 800 tokens (mitigated the queueing hot path)
- Flushed Acme prefix cache and started high-fidelity sampling to capture problematic request traces

Impact: Acme reports throughput restored to ~96% of baseline; error rate reduced from 3.2% -> 0.4% in the last 12h. They are satisfied with immediate mitigation but need assurances for recurrence prevention.

Proposed follow-ups (owner):
- Rishi: implement adaptive concurrency caps by workload size and add per-tenant queueing alerts (2 sprints)
- Evelyn/SRE: add automated warm cache strategies for large-KV paths (1 sprint)
- Marissa/Sean: finalize customer compensation & postmortem (customer-facing incident report)

Ask: leadership visibility for a short customer exec sync tomorrow at 10:00 PT to confirm roadmap/credits. Also recommend we mark this incident as a production reliability priority for the Serving runtime team.

— Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
